ceo_review.outcome: reframe accepted with extended scope (4 of 4 optional items included)

eng_review.key_architecture_finding: StoryCluster.quality_score name collision avoided via distinct content_quality_penalty field

risks_surfaced_by_research: compounding penalty risk on single-source clusters (arch-researcher)
AgentConfig default_factory requirement to avoid breaking existing test constructors (arch-researcher)
no existing OpenAI client mocking precedent in repo (test-analyzer)

issues.description: Task H1 (compounding-penalty regression test) did not name its target test file
Task I labeled as depending on Layer 4 but only actually depends on the pre-existing rejection-log format
issues.resolution: Left as documented Layer 5 for sequencing simplicity; noted dependency is looser than stated

issues.description: Task E acceptance criterion asserted total_score equality across differently-sourced clusters, which is false given scoring.py's source-count-driven terms (frequency_score, source_balance_score, multi-source bonus)
issues.resolution: Rewrote acceptance criteria to isolate content_quality_penalty itself, not total_score

issues.description: Task F referenced an undefined penalty threshold not present in QualityGateConfig, and left skip_reason() branch order with the existing quality_score check unspecified
issues.resolution: Added low_content_quality_skip_threshold to QualityGateConfig (Task A); specified content-quality check runs before the existing quality_score check

issues.description: LLM ambiguous-case batch call had no size cap; production logs show ~150-165 articles/day currently hard-rejected under the old rule, most of which move to the ambiguous bucket under the narrowed hard-reject rule -- an uncapped single call was a real risk on high-junk-volume days, undermining ADR-0003's 'bounded cost' claim
issues.resolution: Added 40-article batch-size cap with chunking and per-article text truncation to Task D and ADR-0003

issues.description: Task E mentioned capping total_score at 'a sane floor' with no value specified and no existing precedent for such a floor in scoring.py
issues.resolution: Dropped the floor language; max_content_quality_penalty cap is the only bound, consistent with existing scoring.py allowing negative total_score

issues.description: MIN-aggregation (one clean article zeroes cluster content_quality_penalty) combines with scoring.py's pre-existing source-count-rewards-credibility mechanics to let a majority-junk cluster (5 junk + 1 clean) fully zero its penalty and outrank a solitary clean single-source report
issues.resolution: User chose junk-fraction-weighted penalty over documenting-as-limitation; switched cluster aggregation from MIN to mean across cluster articles (ADR-0001 updated, Task E rewritten, new acceptance case for 5-junk-1-clean scenario)
